subject: Temporary rate-floor adjustment and capacity sync — NovaHealth pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lucy Patel <lucy@novahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary rate-floor adjustment and capacity sync — NovaHealth pilot

Team — looping you all in for a quick coordinated ask from NovaHealth. They kick off a closed pilot next Tuesday (5/11) and expectation is a concentrated ramp over a 72-hour window (heavy bursts during business hours).

Key asks from the customer: a temporary "rate floor" to avoid repeated throttles for short, high-QPS bursts, and a short-term quota uplift for the pilot window. They specifically asked that we avoid 429s for generator routes that are <250ms latencies.

Attached: novahealth_launch_plan.pdf and novahealth_traffic_forecast.csv (projections by hour). High-level forecast: peak sustained 1200 rps for 3 hours/day, with micro-bursts up to 6k rps lasting <30s. Baseline trial traffic is low outside the launch window.

Asks from Redwood side:
- Neha: feasibility of a temporary rate-floor policy (what safe floor can we set without destabilizing other customers in the region).
- Connor: verification of quota bump mechanics and whether we can carve a short-lived capacity slice for NovaHealth (5/10–5/14).
- Aditya: any billing/credit implications — customer expects a pilot credit for the trial window if we need to issue one for SLA flexibility.

TL;DR: Need an internal decision by EOD Tuesday 5/4 so we can confirm with NovaHealth and finalize the onboarding playbook.

Thanks — K

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: [novahealth_launch_plan.pdf (12 pages), novahealth_traffic_forecast.csv (hourly forecast)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary rate-floor adjustment and capacity sync — NovaHealth pilot

Thanks Kim — reviewed the forecast quickly. A couple of clarifying questions before we commit:

1) By 'rate floor' do they mean a guaranteed minimum per-second throttle allowance (i.e., bypass burst token bucket) or do they want increased concurrency/parallelism for short windows? The mitigation differs.
2) Can NovaHealth accept a slightly relaxed latency SLO during the burst window (e.g., 300ms peak) in exchange for greatly reduced 429s? That option reduces resource pressure.
3) Region: you indicated US — confirm if traffic will come from multiple cloud regions (we can localize capacity if they are regionally distributed).

Prelim: We can implement a temporary policy that favors short bursts by raising the per-customer token bucket refill rate for the generator route and setting a 30s burst allowance. Safest floor I can recommend without wide impact: allow bursts up to 10k tokens over 60s with a sustained cap matching their predicted sustained peak (1.2k rps). That will still require capacity carve-outs if bursts hit 6k+ regularly.

I'll draft the change and run it by infra testing tomorrow. Need Connor to confirm reserved slice availability for 5/10–5/14.

—Neha

Thanks — we can provide a short-lived reserved capacity slice scoped to the NovaHealth account. Notes:

- Recommended reservation: 8 x A100-equivalent slots for peak hours (local region), auto-scaled down outside 09:00–18:00 PST window. This covers sustained 1.2k rps with headroom for bursts if Neha's burst policy is applied.
- Quota bump: we'll issue a temporary quota increase via the quota_change_request_4578.docx (attached). Change window 2026-05-10 00:00 UTC through 2026-05-14 23:59 UTC.
- Operational impact: small, but we need a playbook to fallback to lower-capacity model variants if GPU pressure exceeds the slice (we should pin a smaller quantized variant for fallback).

I'll put in the formal reservation ticket and CC infra on the runbook. Connor

- Need deal manager sign-off (this goes to legal/finance). I'll open a charge approval request and include the proposed credit cap.
- Also confirm whether the quota bump will be reflected as a temporary entitlement in their account (so they don't get automated alerts after 5/14). Connor: can your ticket include automatic rollback?

I'll sync with finance and loop back by EOD.
